extracted.intended_audience: writers of creative nonfiction / personal essayists learning the lyrical essay
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing lyrical essays (a subgenre of personal/creative nonfiction) that blend prose and poetry, use fragmented images and associative logic, and prioritize lyrical language and sensory detail over linear narrative or explicit argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combines prose and poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Combines prose and poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lyrical essay blends elements of prose and poetry; it may be crafted like a prose poem (written in sentences rather than verse) while using poetic devices. Example: Seneca Review definition and the prose-poem form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructed from a distillation of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructed from a distillation of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on concentrated, distilled ideas rather than extended argumentation or narrative exposition. Use small, potent images or observations that accumulate meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentions but doesn’t expound
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions but doesn’t expound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allude to topics, details, or references without fully explaining them; suggestion and implication are preferred to exhaustive explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestive but not exhaustive
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggestive but not exhaustive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The essay should point toward meanings and feelings rather than closing them down; avoid conclusory or fully spelled-out interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relies on associations, imagery, and connotation
rubrics_metrics.description: Relies on associations, imagery, and connotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meaning is generated through associative logic, imagery, and the resonances of words (connotation) instead of linear argument. Use metaphor, simile, and associative leaps to connect fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Makes reference to other genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Makes reference to other genres, such as film, music, literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring in and allude to material from other media or genres (song lyrics, film, literature) as part of the essay’s associative texture; references are often left uncommented to carry suggestive weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arranged in fragments as a mosaic
rubrics_metrics.description: Arranged in fragments as a mosaic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure the piece in fragments or sections that together form a mosaic. Fragments are often separated by white space, double spaces, asterisks, numbers, subtitles, or epigraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Based on stories that are metaphors
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on stories that are metaphors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor the essay in stories or images that function metaphorically; literal events are used for their metaphorical or symbolic resonances rather than as plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Based on intimate voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on intimate voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an intimate, often confiding voice (frequently first person) that conveys emotional truth and subjective perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crafted with lyrical language
rubrics_metrics.description: Crafted with lyrical language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ sound devices and musical phrasing—alliteration, assonance, internal rhyme, cadence—to achieve lyrical prose. The page cites examples like Eula Biss and recommends reading the Seneca Review for models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fragmented structure (use of white space and separators)
rubrics_metrics.description: The essay is created with fragments of details, and each fragment is separated with white space, asterisk, or number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate fragments visually (white space, asterisks, numbers, subtitles) to create pauses and associative jumps. This physical fragmentation supports the essay’s mosaic logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory detail / imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer constructs images with sensory details; description that expresses what the writer sees, hears, smells, tastes, touches, and feels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid sensory description to recreate experience and evoke emotion. Sensory specifics anchor associative fragments and invite reader empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-narrative / non-chronological organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer uses a series of image or ideas, not narrative or argument, to craft the essay; it is not organized as a narrative or in chronological order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid linear plotting or chronological sequencing; let the piece proceed by thematic or associative connections rather than cause–effect storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic devices (alliteration, assonance, internal rhyme)
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer uses poetic language, such as alliteration and assonance and internal rhyme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately incorporate sound patterns and other poetic devices to create musicality in prose. These devices help produce a lyrical tone and should be used intentionally rather than gratuitously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm and sentence pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer crafts sentences that have rhythm, like a prose poem. Paces and stressed syllables determine rhythm; short sentences speed pace, long sentences slow it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to stressed syllables and sentence length to control pace and emotion; the page notes iambic pentameter as a common pattern but advises writers often simply count stressed syllables. Vary sentence length for effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconclusive ending / meditative tone
rubrics_metrics.description: The lyrical essay is often inconclusive; the writer provides no final point for the reader to take away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor endings that invite continued thought rather than resolving everything. The piece should be meditative and encourage reader pondering.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-person / intimate POV
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer often writes in the first person POV (I) and shares intimate details, such as emotional truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an intimate, confessional first-person voice to convey interiority. The page emphasizes answering 'Who does it feel?' rather than objective reportage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figurative language (metaphor and simile)
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer makes comparisons with metaphor and simile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metaphor and simile to create associative links between images and ideas; figurative language is central to the lyricism and meaning-making of the essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connotation over explicit statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer expresses meaning through connotation, not explicit expression of the details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let words carry associative and felt meaning rather than spelling out literal explanation; trust readers to infer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions posed to the reader
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer presents questions and relies on the reader to provide the answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rhetorical or direct questions to engage readers and create spaces for their interpretation; do not feel obliged to answer every question raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Juxtaposition / association of fragments
rubrics_metrics.description: The writer often juxtaposes different fragments of detail, which have implied meaning; association is used to express meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place disparate fragments side-by-side to create new resonances; meaning arises from the relationship between fragments rather than explicit linking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose and poetry / found objects
rubrics_metrics.description: The lyrical essay combines both prose and poetry, sometimes found objects of writing to create the lyrical essay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix prose passages with poetic fragments, quotations, epigraphs, lists, or other 'found' texts. The collage of sources can be a structural and rhetorical strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference without elaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: The lyrical essay often mentions something without elaborating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drop references, names, or moments into the text and allow them to resonate without full explanation—this produces suggestiveness and associative depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of outside voices / shadowing (especially in braided essays)
rubrics_metrics.description: The braided essay allows for an outside voice to provide details, along with the writer’s voice and experiences; the outside voice shadows the writer's voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weave other voices (quotes, interviews, facts, lists) with the primary voice to create interplay and shadowing; repetition of fragments can create a braided texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prose Poem form
rubrics_metrics.description: Prose Poem: crafted like prose but reads like a poem; written in sentences, not verse, with poetic devices such as imagery, symbolism, simile, and metaphor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for paragraph-sized units that behave like poems—intense imagery, tight language, musicality—while retaining sentence syntax rather than line breaks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collage Essay form
rubrics_metrics.description: Collage Essay: based on a collection of fragments from different sources (prose, poetry, quotation) using juxtaposition; sections separated by white space, asterisks, subtitles, or epigraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine heterogeneous materials and let their juxtapositions create meaning; visual separation (spacing, symbols) emphasizes fragmentary collage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Braided Essay form
rubrics_metrics.description: Braided Essay: fragments from different sources repeat and weave throughout the essay; mixing quotations, descriptions, facts, lists, poetic language, imagery, and outside voices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weave several recurring strands (themes, images, voices) throughout the piece so they echo and inform one another; braided repetition creates coherence out of fragments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermit Crab Essay form
rubrics_metrics.description: Hermit Crab Essay: created from the shell of another form—borrows from fiction, poetry, description, personal narrative, instructions, lists, songs, recipes, etc., to construct something new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an existing text or form (a 'shell') as scaffolding for the essay’s own material; repurpose formats like lists, tables of contents, or lyrics as structural devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone: friendly and conversational
rubrics_metrics.description: Tone: A friendly and conversational tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor an approachable, conversational register; avoid overly academic or distancing diction unless deliberately contrasted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word choice: fresh, original, short rather than long
rubrics_metrics.description: Word choice: Fresh and original, short rather than long, familiar instead of unfamiliar words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer vivid, economical diction and fresh phrasing. Use familiar words in original combinations rather than rare vocabulary for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentence variety: Use of a variety of sentence patterns, such as the balanced sentence, the cumulative sentence, and the periodic sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary sentence constructions (short/long, balanced/cumulative/periodic) to control rhythm and maintain reader engagement.
